proposed_reports.title: Yukon Public Accounts (Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis and Consolidated Financial Statements)
proposed_reports.publisher: Yukon Department of Finance / Office of the Comptroller
proposed_reports.description: Annual audited Public Accounts of the Government of Yukon, including the Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis that reports actual revenues (formula financing grant, CHT, CST) and the consolidated financial statements.

proposed_reports.title: Northwest Territories Public Accounts (Consolidated Financial Statements and Financial Highlights)
proposed_reports.description: Annual Public Accounts of the Government of the Northwest Territories, including consolidated financial statements that detail the Territorial Formula Financing Grant, its calculation basis (Gross Expenditure Base, eligible revenues) and the share of total revenue represented by federal transfers.

proposed_reports.title: Nunavut Public Accounts (with Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis)
proposed_reports.description: Annual Public Accounts of the Government of Nunavut, including the Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis that reports actual Territorial Formula Financing receipts and their year-over-year change.

proposed_reports.title: Yukon Statistical Review
proposed_reports.description: Annual statistical compendium prepared by the Yukon Bureau of Statistics covering population, labour force, earnings, CPI, GDP by industry, retail trade, tourism and other indicators, drawing heavily on Statistics Canada data.

dependencies.basis: The Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis of the Yukon Public Accounts states that the majority of revenues come from the formula financing grant and quantifies the federal share of total revenue.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Government’s revenue is largely made up of the formula financing grant from the Government of Canada, which tends to remain stable over time. ... In 2025, the Government received 81.7% of its revenue from the Government of Canada ... In 2025, the Government received $1.350 billion from the formula financing grant, an increase of $98.0 million (7.8%) from the previous year.

dependencies.basis: The Yukon Public Accounts schedule of revenues and the Discussion and Analysis list the Canada Health Transfer as a distinct federal transfer.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Canada Health Transfer was $59.5 million, and the Canada Social Transfer was $19.3 million.

dependencies.basis: The Yukon Public Accounts schedule of revenues and the Discussion and Analysis list the Canada Social Transfer as a distinct federal transfer.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Canada Health Transfer was $59.5 million, and the Canada Social Transfer was $19.3 million.

dependencies.basis: The NWT Public Accounts Consolidated Financial Statements and notes explain the Territorial Formula Financing Grant as the difference between the Gross Expenditure Base and eligible revenues, and report that federal grants and transfer payments constitute 73.1% of revenue.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Territorial Formula Financing Grant is an annual formula-based calculation based on a three-year moving average of data, which includes a two-year lag, to fill the fiscal gap between the Government’s expenditure needs and its ability to raise revenues. The NWT’s Grant equals the difference between its Gross Expenditure Base and a measure of revenue capacity known as eligible revenues. ... The Government’s largest source of revenue is the grant and transfer payments from Canada which represent 73.1% of revenue for the current year.

dependencies.basis: The Nunavut Public Accounts Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis reports the actual Territorial Formula Financing amount and its year-over-year change as the primary driver of federal revenue growth.
